notes: Paper match: arXiv 0806.2320 = Bradač et al. 2008 ApJ 687, 959 (DOI 10.1086/591246); author list matches. Pointer mismatch (minor): in the arXiv source the offsets table is the 2nd table (Table 2, label tab:offset) as pointed, but the lensing analysis is §4 (Mass reconstruction §4.3), the X-ray peak is §5, and Fig. 2 in the arXiv version is the LRIS spectrum; Fig. 4 (fig:kappa) shows kappa/X-ray/light contours with the mass-peak cyan cross. Published-version numbering may differ. No absolute RA/Dec is given for the lensing peak or galaxies; only (Delta x, Delta y) arcmin offsets from the gas peak, so d_IG is directly |offset_I| and d_IS = |offset_I - offset_S| (analyst to compute). The sign convention of Delta x is not stated; only magnitudes/differences matter. The 'galaxies' row is not described as a luminosity-weighted centroid anywhere in the text; no BCG coordinates are tabulated, so under the protocol the S fallback (BCG) has no numeric value in this paper. G uncertainty: Table 2 gives ±0.08 arcmin per axis (=4.8 arcsec), consistent with the §5 statement of 'within 5 arcsec' which the authors treat as a top-hat (not Gaussian) bound. The X-ray peak is a single peak shared by both subclusters (same row 'gas' at 0,0 for SE and NW). Conclusion text: 'There is no significant offset between the peaks of the total mass distribution and the galaxies.'
